name: run

name: text
arguments: CONTROL is a live TEXT-CONTROL, COMBO-BOX or SEARCH-CONTROL. Optional NOTIFY affects writes and is ignored by reads.
description: Read the current UTF-8 text; returned storage survives later native calls. Native positions are not Lisp string indices. COMBO-BOX is single-line: NUL/CR/LF writes reject. Clears old native selection then ChangeValue; matching-text selection readback remains native. SEARCH-CONTROL query is copied native single-line text with NUL/CR/LF write rejection; hint is separate SEARCH-HINT.

setf.description: Text replacement is silent by default. :NOTIFY T emits text-change events synchronously; callback conditions return to the writer caller. Writers are generic functions with VALUE first, followed by the receiver. Values must be strings without NUL; ABI36 validates instead of truncating. Read-only is user typing policy, not a programmatic mutation restriction. COMBO-BOX writes are silent by default; :NOTIFY T emits exactly one :TEXT-CHANGE even unchanged, after commit. Same-combo callback writes reject; callback errors preserve committed text. See docs/COMBO-BOXES.md. SEARCH-CONTROL uses silent ChangeValue by default; notify emits exactly one TEXT event even unchanged. Same-source query/hint writes reject during actual input callbacks; native search/cancel are separate kinds. See docs/SEARCH-CONTROLS.md.

name: selection
arguments: CONTROL is a live CHOICE, LIST-BOX, RADIO-BOX, COMBO-BOX, NOTEBOOK or TREE-CONTROL; NOTIFY is meaningful for the writer only.
returns: Index/NIL for choice/listbox/notebook; non-NIL index for radio-box; canonical TREE-ITEM/NIL for tree-control. COMBO-BOX returns native committed index/NIL, not highlighted popup state.
description: Read current selection: an index for CHOICE/LIST-BOX/NOTEBOOK, or a canonical managed TREE-ITEM view for TREE-CONTROL, with NIL when no selection exists. Reader NOTIFY is ignored. Writes are silent by default; notifying choice/list writes emit synthetic events, while notebook/tree writes use native vetoable selection. Return of a requested assignment does not prove native acceptance. Populated tree writes require a live same-tree item; NIL is empty-tree no-op only. Root creation and structural edits silently normalize valid selection before idle. RADIO-BOX always has exactly one valid index; its explicit notifying write commits before a native-class command event, without veto or rollback. COMBO-BOX selection writes also set item text; NIL clears both text and selection. Arbitrary text writes do not promise a selected item. LIST-CONTROL is fixed single selection, NIL clears; silent by default, :notify T allows actual native selected/deselected events.
scope: Requires an active GUI session on the process main thread. Invalid/destroyed handles or unsupported native arguments signal NATIVE-ERROR; Lisp argument/type errors remain Lisp conditions. Fixed2..64 choices, mandatory valid zero-based selection, one row/column orientation. Active GUI session/native lifetime checks for widget operations; no standalone radio buttons, item mutation or full native parity. See docs/RADIO-GROUPS.md. Also specializes on AUI-NOTEBOOK; empty readNIL, nonempty integer writes only. Silent ChangeSelection versus native notifying/vetoable SetSelection; writer returns request, read actual state. Callback writes reject.
wxwidgets: wxChoice/wxListBox::GetSelection/SetSelection; wxNotebook::GetSelection/ChangeSelection/SetSelection (wxWidgets 3.2.12). wxTreeCtrl::GetSelection/SelectItem in ABI39. wxRadioBox::GetSelection/SetSelection. wxComboBox::GetSelection/SetSelection, wxTextEntry::ChangeValue.

setf.description: For CHOICE: index or NIL for none; silent by default. :NOTIFY T emits one synthetic native choice selection event, including unchanged assignments. For NOTEBOOK: existing integer index only (no NIL); ChangeSelection is silent by default, :NOTIFY T uses native vetoable SetSelection. Same-page notification counts are native/port-dependent. Returns the requested value even when vetoed; read actual selection afterward. LIST-BOX mirrors CHOICE index/NIL behavior, with :LISTBOX-SELECTION text/index/action metadata. Item edits adjust selection silently per LIST-BOX.md. TREE-CONTROL requires a same-tree TREE-ITEM, or NIL only when empty. Native SelectItem is silent by default; :NOTIFY T can be vetoed. Returns the requested view, not proof of acceptance. RADIO-BOX requires a valid non-NIL index; silent by default, :NOTIFY T commits then emits one event even unchanged; same-group callback writes reject, silent other-group writes allowed. COMBO-BOX existing index/NIL only; silent default. :NOTIFY T emits exactly one :COMBO-SELECTION even unchanged/NIL, without extra text notification. Text and selected state commit before callbacks. See docs/COMBO-BOXES.md.

name: event-handler
arguments: Superclass STANDARD-OBJECT. No native initargs; subclasses may add slot initargs and defaults.
returns: A native-backed owned standalone handler, or the base identity of an existing window subclass.
description: Concrete standalone wxEvtHandler wrapper and superclass of WINDOW. Standalone native objects are owned by the application session, explicitly destroyed or automatically freed at session cleanup, without a Lisp GC finalizer. Windows borrow their own native wxWindow base identity and retain window/parent lifetime. Neither case exposes an arbitrary GetEventHandler chain or permits user-supplied native handles. Standalone wrappers are now strongly canonicalized by session identity for EQ chain peer lookup; no new native ownership or finalizer is introduced. Managed window push leaves native ownership/session rooting unchanged; window destruction detaches handlers rather than deleting them.

Invalid/stale native handles signal NATIVE-ERROR except HANDLER-ALIVE-P, which returns NIL for destroyed/unknown IDs during an active session. Unsupported Lisp receivers use CLOS dispatch errors. Generic observer/contextual bindings cover built-ins and registered command/notify names, including on the borrowed application view. Arbitrary native classes, validated OS session delivery, pushed handler chains and native virtual overrides remain unbound. Construction rollback releases created resources/roots but does not undo arbitrary external chain edits; native destruction splices survivors around the failed node.

Destroying a linked standalone handler during a callback now rejects; outside callbacks native destruction splices reciprocal neighbors. Unlinked callback destruction retains existing deferral. Attached handlers are removed from their managed window before outside-callback deletion; linked/attached callback destruction rejects.

arguments: OBJECT is any Lisp value.

description: Type predicate only; does not query native registration and needs no active session.
scope: No native session required. This predicate says nothing about whether a binding remains active.

name: bind-event
arguments: HANDLER is an EVENT-HANDLER/window; KIND is :CLICK, :TEXT-CHANGE, :TOGGLE, :SELECTION, :CLOSE, :QUERY-END-SESSION, :END-SESSION, :IDLE, :MENU or a registered command/notify name. FUNCTION takes one immutable EVENT. ID defaults NIL (any); LAST-ID defaults NIL (exact ID when ID is given). WITH-CONTEXT defaults NIL; when true FUNCTION takes (EVENT CONTEXT) instead of just EVENT. USER-DATA defaults NIL and associates any EQ-preserved Lisp value with this registration; callback arity is unchanged.
description: Register an observer without replacing any existing generic or control-specific registration. Signed 32-bit IDs are supported except -1 (reserved as native wxID_ANY; use NIL). LAST-ID requires ID and an ordered inclusive range. Observer bindings automatically Skip; contextual bindings start unskipped and control native Skip explicitly; relative callback order follows wxWidgets and is not a Lisp API guarantee. Failed registration releases temporary roots. Contextual access is limited to the innermost callback and expires at return, including on errors. A native entry-owned wxObject token adapter represents non-NIL user data without a Lisp/native pointer. EVENT-USER-DATA reads the per-binding value in snapshots/current contexts; there is no public mutation API for an existing association. ABI37 adds :NOTEBOOK-PAGE-CHANGING/:NOTEBOOK-PAGE-CHANGED notify-family observers/contexts. Only CHANGING veto affects navigation. Native page callbacks protect the originating book/ancestors and reject same-book recursive selection, modal and clipboard entry. ABI38 listbox selection/double-click command events carry cached string/index payloads; snapshots are independent of later item edits. Native list callback guards protect receiver/ancestors and defer modal/clipboard entry while allowing item edits. ABI39 tree selection changing/changed are native-only wxTreeEvent notify types. EVENT-TREE-ITEM captures canonical view identity, not frozen text/validity; same-tree writes and nested native loops defer until callback return. Native report-list and tree interaction kinds documented in REPORT-TREE-VIEWS are readonly notify payloads; expansion/collapse veto is available only for native before-events. No owned/synthetic/cloned views events.
scope: Active main-thread GUI session required; otherwise NATIVE-ERROR. Stale/deleting receivers reject registration/queuing. Invalid event kinds, IDs and payload options signal Lisp errors; wrong receiver types use CLOS dispatch errors. Built-ins and registered command/notify types. Contexts support scoped Skip/propagation and checked close/notify veto. Arbitrary native events, native control-specific notify subclasses, arbitrary native userData pointers, external handler adoption and worker-thread dispatch remain unbound. Session bindings accept only the borrowed application view or an isolated owned handler; windows reject. Real OS delivery remains unverified. Skipped application END_SESSION callbacks can reach process-exiting defaults. Session bindings on attached pushed handlers reject so a window tail cannot route them to app defaults. Callback-local roots preserve current user data after self/peer unbind until return. Snapshots preserve the EQ reference after unbind/session end, not a deep copy of mutable contents. RADIO-BOX :radio-selection is a native-only command kind with copied/current index and native label metadata. Snapshot reads survive source/session cleanup; borrowed contexts require the exact innermost current callback. No owned/synthetic/cloned radio events. See docs/RADIO-GROUPS.md. :TOGGLE-BUTTON-CHANGE copies native checked/text metadata (text normally empty, including explicit notify; no inferred label); no owned/synthetic/clone. Snapshots survive cleanup, contexts expire. See docs/TOGGLE-BUTTONS.md. COMBO-BOX uses new native-only :COMBO-SELECTION and existing :TEXT-CHANGE. Physical native selections may emit multiple command/text notifications; explicit setters emit only their requested kind. See docs/COMBO-BOXES.md. WEB-VIEW adds native-only :WEB-MESSAGE, :WEB-SCRIPT-RESULT, :WEB-LOADED and :WEB-ERROR command snapshots with read-only payloads. JSON messages accept all frames/origins and carry no authentication; script result EVENT-EXTRA-LONG identifies its ticket and EVENT-INTEGER reports success1/error0. No owned/synthetic/cloned web events. GRID exposes selected immutable native notify event kinds160..170, scoped native validation and copied current cell values; see docs/GRID-EDITING.md. See docs/WEB-VIEW.md and docs/GRID.md. Native-only notify AUI100..104 kinds :aui-page-changing/:aui-page-changed/:aui-page-close/:aui-page-closed/:aui-drag-done. Selection/oldselection/targetID copied; payload writers and owned/synthetic/cloned forms reject. Scoped changing/close veto; closed index is former index, not current page. See docs/AUI-NOTEBOOK.md. ABI57 raw key/mouse/focus/context-menu/size, STC and AUI native kinds have copied read-only payload metadata and reject owned/synthetic construction/cloning. Ordinary observers automatically Skip; scoped handlers explicitly Skip unhandled native input. STC styling has the exact innermost same-control STYLENEEDED StartStyling/SetStyling exception. AUI close/changing veto is native-scoped and CLOSED has former index/captured target ID. See docs/INPUT-EVENTS.md, docs/STYLED-TEXT.md and docs/AUI-NOTEBOOK.md. AUI private tab-local PAGE_CHANGING events are translated by native wxAuiNotebook before Lisp delivery; public event-selection uses global catalogue indices. DRAG-DONE follows native paths/early returns without an exact count or ordering-transaction guarantee. AUI/native input/STC context IDs and timestamps are read-only. ABI58 :THREAD is a native base-family wxThreadEvent with copied immutable EVENT-TEXT, GUI-only callback dispatch and normal context lifetime. QUEUE-THREAD-EVENT alone permits worker posting after GUI binding; other GUI operations retain their thread rules. No owned/synthetic/cloned :THREAD events. See docs/THREAD-EVENTS.md.
wxwidgets: wxEvtHandler::Bind member-method overload with wxEvent receiver and optional entry-owned numeric wxObject userData adapter; built-ins and registered command/notify tags (wxWidgets 3.2.12 baseline).
syntax: (wxlambda:bind-event handler kind function &key id last-id with-context user-data)

name: unbind-event
arguments: BINDING is an EVENT-BINDING.
returns: T if this active registration was removed; NIL if already unbound or receiver expired.
description: Remove exactly one registration, including from inside itself or another callback. The current callback may finish; later deliveries cannot invoke the removed function. Releases generic callback roots. A live native binding object is retained until an active callback returns. Unbinding destroys the native user-data adapter and releases global association roots, but active dispatch frames and saved snapshots can keep the Lisp value alive.
scope: Active main-thread GUI session required; otherwise NATIVE-ERROR. Stale/deleting receivers reject registration/queuing. Invalid event kinds, IDs and payload options signal Lisp errors; wrong receiver types use CLOS dispatch errors. Built-ins and registered command/notify types. Contexts support scoped Skip/propagation and checked close/notify veto. Arbitrary native events, native control-specific notify subclasses, arbitrary native userData pointers, external handler adoption and worker-thread dispatch remain unbound.
wxwidgets: wxEvtHandler::Unbind member-method overload, exact receiver/type/ID-range/native binding identity (wxWidgets 3.2.12 baseline).

name: binding-active-p
arguments: BINDING is an EVENT-BINDING.
returns: T if still registered on a live receiver, NIL after unbinding or receiver destruction/requested disposal.
description: Query active-session registration and reap stale generic callback roots. Root pruning also runs at returned RUN/pump/notifying-setter boundaries and after explicit destruction. During a blocking RUN, native window closure may retain roots until a Lisp boundary or explicit unbinding. This does not change the control-specific callback-root contract.
scope: Active main-thread GUI session required; otherwise NATIVE-ERROR. Stale/deleting receivers reject registration/queuing. Invalid event kinds, IDs and payload options signal Lisp errors; wrong receiver types use CLOS dispatch errors. Built-ins and registered command/notify types. Contexts support scoped Skip/propagation and checked close/notify veto. Arbitrary native events, native control-specific notify subclasses, arbitrary native userData pointers, external handler adoption and worker-thread dispatch remain unbound.
wxwidgets: Bridge registration/weak-lifetime predicate for wxEvtHandler bindings.

name: queue-event
arguments: HANDLER is live; KIND is a built-in keyword or registered name. ID defaults 0; TEXT defaults empty. CHECKED-P is toggle/menu-only; SELECTION is NIL/nonnegative index for selection. CAN-VETO-P is close-family-only (default T). Registered types accept signed INTEGER (default 0) and copied TEXT; registered notify types accept initial VETOED-P (default NIL). LOGGING-OFF-P defaults NIL and is accepted only for :QUERY-END-SESSION/:END-SESSION; CAN-VETO-P applies to all close-family kinds. The second positional argument may instead be a live OWNED-EVENT, with no payload keyword overrides.
description: Queue a copied synthetic event: wxCommandEvent for seven command kinds, wxCloseEvent for close/session kinds and wxIdleEvent for :IDLE. Ordinary control properties are not changed directly. A queued close on a frame may run its native default closing action; use CLOSE-WINDOW for a synchronous acceptance result. Explicit UTF-8 lengths preserve text. Close events take no command payload, may be vetoable or non-vetoable, and do not normally propagate to parents. Registry types create wxCommandEvent or wxNotifyEvent according to their declared family. Initial veto applies only to custom notify types. Queuing offers no final veto/handled result; use PROCESS-EVENT when a synchronous decision is required. Owned-event dispatch always clones, attaches the receiver as copy origin and never consumes or mutates the source. The original can be destroyed after queueing or inside callbacks. Processing returns final state from its copy; contextual CLONE-EVENT can retain changed state detached from origin.
scope: Active main-thread GUI session required; otherwise NATIVE-ERROR. Stale/deleting receivers reject registration/queuing. Invalid event kinds, IDs and payload options signal Lisp errors; wrong receiver types use CLOS dispatch errors. Built-ins and registered command/notify types. Contexts support scoped Skip/propagation and checked close/notify veto. Arbitrary native events, native control-specific notify subclasses, arbitrary native userData pointers, external handler adoption and worker-thread dispatch remain unbound. Synthetic session kinds require isolated owned standalone handlers; application/window receivers reject before emission. Standalone session fallback to wxApp is suppressed even for skipped, disabled or unmatched delivery. Native application session bindings are distinct from synthetic probes. Owned session event copies retain isolated standalone-receiver guards. Copies carrying borrowed userdata/client pointers or unsupported exact native classes reject. Copied owned :TEXT-CHANGE delivery to text-entry receivers rejects before emission, preventing lazy GetString from shadowing the owned payload. Keyword synthetic behavior is unchanged. Managed standalone chains participate in native traversal; linking does not change pending queue ownership or introduce window/app pushed chains. Window receivers retain wxEvtHandler semantics and bypass pushed stacks; explicit PROCESS-WINDOW-EVENT/LOCALLY provide stack-aware synchronous routing. Synthetic session delivery to attached pushed handlers rejects before emission/transfer. Notebook native page events cannot be synthesized, queued, processed as owned events or contextually cloned in ABI37. ABI38 simple listbox command kinds support owned/synthetic dispatch and text/selection payloads; no automatic list-model mutation. Derived tree selection kinds cannot be synthesized/owned/cloned in ABI39. ABI58 :THREAD is a native base-family wxThreadEvent with copied immutable EVENT-TEXT, GUI-only callback dispatch and normal context lifetime. QUEUE-THREAD-EVENT alone permits worker posting after GUI binding; other GUI operations retain their thread rules. No owned/synthetic/cloned :THREAD events. See docs/THREAD-EVENTS.md. LIST-CONTROL inherits supported WINDOW operations; owner/ancestor writes defer during native virtual providers.
wxwidgets: wxEvtHandler::QueueEvent; wxCommandEvent, wxCloseEvent or wxIdleEvent construction, SetCanVeto at close-event creation only.
syntax:
(wxlambda:queue-event handler kind &key id text checked-p selection can-veto-p integer vetoed-p logging-off-p)
(wxlambda:queue-event handler owned-event)

name: event-id
arguments: EVENT is an immutable snapshot or current innermost context. SETF VALUE is a signed 32-bit integer, including -1. A live OWNED-EVENT is also accepted for applicable operations.
returns: Captured/current native integer ID; SETF returns VALUE.
description: Read a saved pre-callback ID or current native GetId. Context SETF changes event metadata and later native ID matching, not the source window ID or binding filters. Earlier snapshots stay unchanged. No dispatch restart or callback-order guarantee.
scope: Saved snapshots need no native session. Current reads/writes require an active main-thread session and innermost callback; stale/suspended contexts signal NATIVE-ERROR. Invalid SETF values signal TYPE-ERROR. Context SetId permits -1; binding filters/synthetic initial IDs still reserve it. Native types/origin mutation remain unbound. Live OWNED-EVENT receivers are also supported under the same native field/family validation. They require an active main-thread session and remain mutable until destroyed; snapshots stay immutable. Native ABI57 raw input, STC and AUI context IDs/timestamps are read-only; their SETF writers reject.
wxwidgets: wxEvent::GetId / SetId, signed native int (wxWidgets 3.2.12 baseline).

setf.description: Assign current native ID and return VALUE. Later exact/range matching uses the changed ID; -1 remains literal event metadata and unfiltered bindings still match. No snapshot writer. Also accepts a live OWNED-EVENT under the same field/family restrictions; owned writes change the reusable resource, not copies already dispatched.

name: event-context
arguments: Opaque read-only token value passed as the second argument by BIND-EVENT :WITH-CONTEXT T. No public constructor.
returns: A borrowed callback-scoped native wxEvent view.
description: The context token is immutable; operations mutate the live native event only during its exact innermost callback. Nested contextual callbacks suspend outer access; nested observer/control callbacks also deny outer access. The outer context becomes usable again after nesting returns. Unbinding or deferred receiver disposal does not prematurely expire the running callback context. :CLOSE contexts allow checked veto access; command contexts do not have close-veto state.
scope: Requires an active main-thread session and the innermost currently executing contextual callback. Expired or outer contexts in nested callbacks signal NATIVE-ERROR for native access. Activity queries return NIL for those contexts during a session; outside a session they signal NATIVE-ERROR. No raw native event pointer escapes. Built-ins and registered command/notify types. Veto applies only to actual wxCloseEvent/wxNotifyEvent contexts; arbitrary event types, general event construction/cloning and native control-specific subclasses and validated OS session delivery remains open.
wxwidgets: Borrowed wxEvent base view, four wxCommandEvent tags (wxWidgets 3.2.12 baseline).

name: event-context-p
arguments: OBJECT is any Lisp value.
returns: T for EVENT-CONTEXT values, NIL otherwise.
description: Type predicate only; a saved expired context still satisfies it. No native access or active session is needed.
scope: No active native session required. Use EVENT-CONTEXT-ACTIVE-P for current callback usability.

name: event-context-active-p
arguments: CONTEXT is an EVENT-CONTEXT value.
returns: T only for the current innermost native callback context; NIL for expired/suspended contexts in an active session.
description: Check scoped usability without dereferencing an expired pointer. Observer/control callbacks do not gain access to an enclosing context. The predicate does not assert receiver liveness and remains T during deferred receiver disposal until callback return.
scope: Requires an active main-thread session and the innermost currently executing contextual callback. Expired or outer contexts in nested callbacks signal NATIVE-ERROR for native access. Activity queries return NIL for those contexts during a session; outside a session they signal NATIVE-ERROR. No raw native event pointer escapes. Built-ins and registered command/notify types. Veto applies only to actual wxCloseEvent/wxNotifyEvent contexts; arbitrary event types, general event construction/cloning and native control-specific subclasses and validated OS session delivery remains open.
wxwidgets: Bridge scope/depth validation of borrowed wxEvent access.

name: event-skipped-p
arguments: CONTEXT is the current event context. SETF VALUE is a generalized boolean. A live OWNED-EVENT is also accepted for applicable operations.
returns: Native Skip flag as T/NIL; SETF returns the supplied value.
description: Contextual bindings begin with Skip false. Assign true to continue to later native handlers and normal parent routing; false consumes the command at this handler. This is distinct from propagation level. Mutation is not rolled back on callback errors. Observer bindings without a context retain automatic Skip.
scope: Requires an active main-thread session and the innermost currently executing contextual callback. Expired or outer contexts in nested callbacks signal NATIVE-ERROR for native access. setf.description: Set the native Skip flag only while CONTEXT is current. A true value continues dispatch; returning from a contextual callback does not automatically override the flag. Also accepts a live OWNED-EVENT under the same field/family restrictions; owned writes change the reusable resource, not copies already dispatched.

returns: T when the native propagation level is positive, otherwise NIL.

arguments: EVENT is an immutable snapshot or current innermost event context. SETF VALUE is a signed32 native type returned by EVENT-TYPE for a registered name. A live OWNED-EVENT is also accepted for applicable operations.
description: Read copied/current GetEventType. Saved values remain data after callback/source/session cleanup. Compare to EVENT-TYPE in the same active session; numeric tags are not stable serialized IDs or native cast authority. Context SETF accepts only registered same-family source/target tags and validates actual native command/notify class before SetEventType. Earlier snapshots and registration identities remain unchanged; later snapshots report the current native tag. No dispatch restart or local delivery-order guarantee.
scope: Saved snapshots need no session. Current reads/writes require active main-thread session and innermost callback; stale/suspended contexts signal NATIVE-ERROR. SETF rejects built-in/session/unknown/cross-family types before mutation. Malformed integers signal TYPE-ERROR. Arbitrary tag mutation, class replacement and native ownership remain unbound. Live OWNED-EVENT receivers are also supported under the same native field/family validation. They require an active main-thread session and remain mutable until destroyed; snapshots stay immutable.

setf.description: Assign a registered same-family native type after actual-class checks; return VALUE. Built-in/session sources or targets reject. No snapshot writer, rebind, dispatch restart or local callback-order guarantee. Also accepts a live OWNED-EVENT under the same field/family restrictions; owned writes change the reusable resource, not copies already dispatched.

name: event-type
arguments: KIND is a built-in event keyword or a name registered in this active session.
returns: The corresponding process-local native wxEventType integer.
description: Look up a process-local native type ID. Twenty-two built-in kinds plus registered command/notify names are supported. Registry names are session-scoped; saved snapshot native IDs remain plain data after cleanup. Borrowed application handler access is supported; arbitrary native event-class binding and OS session delivery remains unverified.

RADIO-BOX :radio-selection is a native-only command kind with copied/current index and native label metadata. Snapshot reads survive source/session cleanup; borrowed contexts require the exact innermost current callback. No owned/synthetic/cloned radio events. See docs/RADIO-GROUPS.md. Includes wxEVT_SPLITTER_SASH_POS_CHANGING/CHANGED, wxEVT_SLIDER, wxEVT_SPINCTRL and wxEVT_RADIOBOX (wxWidgets3.2.12). wxEVT_TOGGLEBUTTON. wxEVT_COMBOBOX.

name: event-family
arguments: EVENT is an immutable snapshot, current context or live OWNED-EVENT.
description: Read captured/current supported native classification :COMMAND/:NOTIFY/:CLOSE/:IDLE, including owned event values and saved snapshots after registry cleanup. It is bounded class metadata, not arbitrary native RTTI.
scope: Saved snapshots need no session. Owned/current reads require active main-thread session and valid native lifetime; contexts require the innermost callback. ABI58 :THREAD is a native base-family wxThreadEvent with copied immutable EVENT-TEXT, GUI-only callback dispatch and normal context lifetime. QUEUE-THREAD-EVENT alone permits worker posting after GUI binding; other GUI operations retain their thread rules. No owned/synthetic/cloned :THREAD events. See docs/THREAD-EVENTS.md.
wxwidgets: Portable classification of supported wxCommandEvent/wxNotifyEvent/wxCloseEvent/wxIdleEvent classes (wxWidgets 3.2.12 baseline).

name: event-can-veto-p
arguments: EVENT is a saved snapshot or current event context. SETF requires a current close-family context; VALUE is a generalized boolean. A live OWNED-EVENT is also accepted for applicable operations.
returns: T for veto-capable captured/current close or notify events; NIL otherwise.
description: Snapshots read copied capability without a session. Current close contexts use CanVeto; current notify contexts always support Veto/Allow. Plain command contexts return NIL. Scope validation remains required for native access. Context SETF maps native SetCanVeto directly, including false to true. GetVeto hides a stored veto when CanVeto is false and reveals it again if re-enabled. Forced close starts false but explicit metadata mutation can affect native closing results; OS veto acceptance is not guaranteed.
scope: Active main-thread session required for native context or frame operations. Expired/suspended contexts and invalid/deleting frames signal NATIVE-ERROR. Saved snapshots need no session. Close and registered notify families permit checked veto. Other native control-specific notify subclasses, validated OS session delivery and arbitrary event classes remain open. Live OWNED-EVENT receivers are also supported under the same native field/family validation. They require an active main-thread session and remain mutable until destroyed; snapshots stay immutable.
wxwidgets: wxCloseEvent::CanVeto / SetCanVeto; intrinsic wxNotifyEvent capability is read-only (wxWidgets 3.2.12 baseline).

setf.description: Assign current wxCloseEvent capability, returning VALUE. Snapshot, command and notify writers reject; stale/suspended contexts reject native access. Does not clear the native stored veto bit or guarantee OS policy. Also accepts a live OWNED-EVENT under the same field/family restrictions; owned writes change the reusable resource, not copies already dispatched.

name: event-vetoed-p
arguments: EVENT is a saved snapshot or current close/notify context. SETF requires a current veto-capable context. A live OWNED-EVENT is also accepted for applicable operations.
returns: Copied/current veto state as T/NIL; SETF returns the supplied generalized boolean.
description: Snapshots retain pre-callback state. Close contexts use GetVeto / checked Veto(bool); notify contexts use NOT IsAllowed, Veto() for true, and Allow() for NIL. A close initialized non-vetoable rejects writes unless its current CanVeto flag was explicitly enabled through SETF EVENT-CAN-VETO-P. Plain command contexts reject live veto-state access. Snapshots stay immutable. Native GetVeto is CanVeto AND the stored veto bit; disabling capability hides the bit without clearing it.
scope: Active main-thread session required for native context or frame operations. Expired/suspended contexts and invalid/deleting frames signal NATIVE-ERROR. Saved snapshots need no session. Close and registered notify families permit checked veto. Other native control-specific notify subclasses, validated OS session delivery and arbitrary event classes remain open. Live OWNED-EVENT receivers are also supported under the same native field/family validation. They require an active main-thread session and remain mutable until destroyed; snapshots stay immutable.
wxwidgets: wxCloseEvent::GetVeto / Veto(bool); wxNotifyEvent::IsAllowed / Veto / Allow. (wxWidgets 3.2.12 baseline).

setf.description: Close contexts require CanVeto true before either assignment. Notify true invokes Veto and NIL invokes Allow. Plain command contexts and stale/suspended contexts reject access; snapshots have no SETF method. Also accepts a live OWNED-EVENT under the same field/family restrictions; owned writes change the reusable resource, not copies already dispatched.

name: close-window
arguments: FRAME is a live FRAME. Optional FORCE defaults NIL; true initializes native CanVeto false.
returns: Native close acceptance as T/NIL; not a destruction/liveness guarantee.
description: Synchronously generate the frame close request via wxWindow::Close(force). A vetoed request returns NIL. A consuming contextual callback may return acceptance T without deleting anything, even for FORCE. Set Skip true to delegate to native default closing when appropriate. Callback conditions re-signal at this Lisp boundary; a handled nested condition does not stop RUN. Use DESTROY-WINDOW for explicit destruction. A callback can explicitly mutate CanVeto through SETF EVENT-CAN-VETO-P; FORCE is not an immutable capability limit.
scope: Active main-thread session required for native context or frame operations. Expired/suspended contexts and invalid/deleting frames signal NATIVE-ERROR. Saved snapshots need no session. Close and registered notify families permit checked veto. Other native control-specific notify subclasses, validated OS session delivery and arbitrary event classes remain open. Closing a protected active-modal ancestor rejects until SHOW-MODAL returns; modal dialog close itself uses cancellation.

name: register-event-type
arguments: NAME is a unique keyword not reserved by a built-in kind. FAMILY is :NOTIFY (default) or :COMMAND.
description: Allocate a process-local native event type and map NAME in the active session. Duplicate names, built-ins and unsupported families are rejected before registration. Names cannot be unregistered or replaced during this session. Registrations are session-wide metadata, not rolled back when an unrelated resource initializer fails. Native type IDs are not stable across processes.
scope: Active main-thread session required for registration/dispatch and scoped native access; inactive calls signal NATIVE-ERROR before FFI. Wrong receiver types use CLOS dispatch errors. Registry metadata lasts until session cleanup; snapshot data is immutable. Borrowed application dispatch is supported; no worker dispatch, validated OS session delivery or arbitrary native class construction is provided.
wxwidgets: wxNewEventType; synthetic wxCommandEvent/wxNotifyEvent family registration (wxWidgets 3.2.12 baseline).

name: process-event
arguments: HANDLER is a live EVENT-HANDLER/window. KIND and keyword payloads match QUEUE-EVENT. LOGGING-OFF-P defaults NIL and is accepted only for :QUERY-END-SESSION/:END-SESSION; CAN-VETO-P applies to all close-family kinds. The second positional argument may instead be a live OWNED-EVENT, with no payload keyword overrides.
returns: Two values: native handled-p and final vetoed-p.
description: Synchronously dispatch a fresh owned synthetic event through ProcessEvent, copy final veto state and then delete the event. Observer callbacks may run while handled-p is NIL because they Skip; native consumption/default handling determines the first result. Final veto is independent of handled-p and may be true from initial VETOED-P even without a matching handler. Close dispatch can run frame defaults. Callback errors re-signal at the nearer Lisp boundary; handled nested errors do not stop RUN. No final values are returned when a condition escapes, and earlier callback mutations are not rolled back. Owned-event dispatch always clones, attaches the receiver as copy origin and never consumes or mutates the source. The original can be destroyed after queueing or inside callbacks. Processing returns final state from its copy; contextual CLONE-EVENT can retain changed state detached from origin.
scope: Active main-thread session required for registration/dispatch and scoped native access; inactive calls signal NATIVE-ERROR before FFI. Wrong receiver types use CLOS dispatch errors. Registry metadata lasts until session cleanup; snapshot data is immutable. Borrowed application dispatch is supported; no worker dispatch, validated OS session delivery or arbitrary native class construction is provided. Synthetic session kinds require isolated owned standalone handlers; application/window receivers reject before emission. Standalone session fallback to wxApp is suppressed even for skipped, disabled or unmatched delivery. Native application session bindings are distinct from synthetic probes. Owned session event copies retain isolated standalone-receiver guards. Copies carrying borrowed userdata/client pointers or unsupported exact native classes reject. Copied owned :TEXT-CHANGE delivery to text-entry receivers rejects before emission, preventing lazy GetString from shadowing the owned payload. Keyword synthetic behavior is unchanged. Managed standalone chains participate in native traversal; linking does not change pending queue ownership or introduce window/app pushed chains. Window receivers retain wxEvtHandler semantics and bypass pushed stacks; explicit PROCESS-WINDOW-EVENT/LOCALLY provide stack-aware synchronous routing. Synthetic session delivery to attached pushed handlers rejects before emission/transfer. Notebook native page events cannot be synthesized, queued, processed as owned events or contextually cloned in ABI37. ABI38 simple listbox command kinds support owned/synthetic dispatch and text/selection payloads; no automatic list-model mutation. Derived tree selection kinds cannot be synthesized/owned/cloned in ABI39. LIST-CONTROL inherits supported WINDOW operations; owner/ancestor writes defer during native virtual providers.
wxwidgets: wxEvtHandler::ProcessEvent; wxCloseEvent::GetVeto or NOT wxNotifyEvent::IsAllowed after dispatch. (wxWidgets 3.2.12 baseline).
syntax:
(wxlambda:process-event handler kind &key id text checked-p selection can-veto-p integer vetoed-p logging-off-p)
(wxlambda:process-event handler owned-event)

name: event-integer
arguments: EVENT is a snapshot, current context or live OWNED-EVENT. SETF VALUE is signed32 and requires command/notify state.
returns: Captured/current native command integer; zero for close/idle-family reads. SETF returns VALUE.
description: Read GetInt or change the native command payload with SETF. Built-in toggle/selection interpretations can reflect this underlying value. Earlier snapshots remain unchanged. Raw values can affect semantic checked/selection views; negative indices other than -1 remain visible through EVENT-SELECTION after raw writes. It does not alter EXTRA-LONG or raw IsSelection.
scope: Saved reads need no session. Live access requires active main-thread session and valid owned/innermost-context lifetime. Close-family writes reject; malformed/out-of-range values signal TYPE-ERROR. WEB-VIEW :WEB-MESSAGE/:WEB-SCRIPT-RESULT/:WEB-LOADED/:WEB-ERROR payload contexts are read-only: text/integer/extra-LONG SETF reject. Script results carry JSON or error text, success1/error0 in EVENT-INTEGER and ticket in EVENT-EXTRA-LONG; messages carry JSON without sender authentication. See docs/WEB-VIEW.md. ABI57 raw key/mouse/focus/context-menu/size, STC and AUI native kinds have copied read-only payload metadata and reject owned/synthetic construction/cloning. Ordinary observers automatically Skip; scoped handlers explicitly Skip unhandled native input. STC styling has the exact innermost same-control STYLENEEDED StartStyling/SetStyling exception. AUI close/changing veto is native-scoped and CLOSED has former index/captured target ID. See docs/INPUT-EVENTS.md, docs/STYLED-TEXT.md and docs/AUI-NOTEBOOK.md.

setf.description: Assign a signed32 native command/notify payload and return VALUE. No snapshot writer; stale contexts and destroyed resources reject.

name: application-handler
arguments: No public constructor; obtain the session view with CURRENT-APPLICATION-HANDLER.
returns: An EVENT-HANDLER subclass representing the managed wxApp.
description: Borrowed native identity with inherited binding, dispatch, liveness and enabled state. Direct construction and subclass construction are rejected; explicit destruction signals NATIVE-ERROR. Session cleanup owns the native wxApp.
scope: One cached view in the active main-thread session. No native wxApp subclassing, replacement or ownership transfer; native session bindings exist but OS delivery remains unverified. Saved views reject native access outside the session.
wxwidgets: wxApp / wxAppConsole::GetInstance and wxTheApp, managed instance only (wxWidgets 3.2.12 baseline).

construction.description: Obtain the cached borrowed application view. Direct MAKE-INSTANCE, subclass construction and MAKE-EVENT-HANDLER construction are forbidden; only session cleanup owns native wxApp destruction.

name: current-application-handler
arguments: None.
returns: The EQ-identical APPLICATION-HANDLER view for the current session.
description: Borrow the bridge application event handler without constructing or taking ownership of wxApp. Native main-thread/session validation runs on every lookup, including cached lookups.
scope: Active main-thread session required; otherwise NATIVE-ERROR. One session per process. No external application adoption; native session bindings exist but OS delivery remains unverified.
wxwidgets: wxAppConsole::GetInstance / wxTheApp, bridge-managed application only (wxWidgets 3.2.12 baseline).

name: event-logging-off-p
arguments: EVENT is a saved session-event snapshot or current innermost session-event context. SETF VALUE is a generalized boolean. A live OWNED-EVENT is also accepted for applicable operations.
returns: T for logging off, NIL for system shutdown; SETF returns VALUE.
description: Read copied or current wxCloseEvent logging-off metadata for :QUERY-END-SESSION/:END-SESSION. Context SETF changes native metadata only, not OS policy. Snapshots retain pre-callback state and have no SETF method.
scope: Saved session snapshots require no session. Non-session snapshots signal Lisp errors; non-session, stale or suspended contexts signal NATIVE-ERROR. Native access requires an active main-thread session. OS session delivery is not validated by isolated synthetic tests. Live OWNED-EVENT receivers are also supported under the same native field/family validation. They require an active main-thread session and remain mutable until destroyed; snapshots stay immutable.

setf.description: Assign the current native session flag, returning the generalized boolean. No snapshot writer; no OS logout/shutdown action is performed. Also accepts a live OWNED-EVENT under the same field/family restrictions; owned writes change the reusable resource, not copies already dispatched.

name: event-timestamp
arguments: EVENT is an immutable snapshot or current event context. SETF VALUE must fit signed native C long. A live OWNED-EVENT is also accepted for applicable operations.
returns: Native millisecond timestamp as a Lisp integer; SETF returns VALUE.
description: Read copied/current native timestamp, not necessarily Unix time. Negative values including -1 are valid. Synthetic events start at zero. Context SETF changes metadata only, not scheduling. Snapshots stay immutable and preserve pre-callback values.
scope: Saved snapshot reads need no native session. Context access requires an active main-thread session and the innermost callback; expired/suspended contexts signal NATIVE-ERROR. Malformed/out-of-range SETF values signal TYPE-ERROR. Native LONG width is platform-specific; mouse/key events are not yet bound. Live OWNED-EVENT receivers are also supported under the same native field/family validation. They require an active main-thread session and remain mutable until destroyed; snapshots stay immutable. Native ABI57 raw input, STC and AUI context IDs/timestamps are read-only; their SETF writers reject.
wxwidgets: wxEvent::GetTimestamp / SetTimestamp, native signed long widened to int64_t at the ABI (wxWidgets 3.2.12 baseline).

setf.description: Assign a signed native LONG timestamp to the current event. No snapshot writer or synthetic-constructor timestamp keyword. No Unix-epoch or scheduling meaning is implied. Also accepts a live OWNED-EVENT under the same field/family restrictions; owned writes change the reusable resource, not copies already dispatched.

name: event-command-p
arguments: EVENT is an immutable snapshot or current event context. A live OWNED-EVENT is also accepted for applicable operations.
returns: T for native command/notify-derived events; NIL for close/idle-family events.
description: Read captured/current native IsCommandEvent classification. No mutable classification or event replacement. Saved values remain independent of source lifetime.
scope: Saved snapshots need no session. Current-context access requires an active main-thread session and the innermost callback; stale/suspended contexts signal NATIVE-ERROR. No SETF writer. Live OWNED-EVENT receivers are also supported under the same native field/family validation. They require an active main-thread session and remain mutable until destroyed; snapshots stay immutable.

name: event-origin-id
arguments: EVENT is an immutable snapshot, current innermost context or live OWNED-EVENT. SETF accepts only NIL on live state under the bounded detachment rules.
returns: Positive opaque bridge identity, or NIL for null/untracked native origin.
description: Copy/read GetEventObject identity only when it matches a registered application, owned handler, tracked window or managed menu resource. This differs from EVENT-SOURCE (binding receiver) and EVENT-ID (routing metadata). Pointer identity is compared without dereferencing the origin; no native pointer or wrapper reconstruction is exposed. Clear-only live SETF accepts NIL. Owned events are already detached; non-null current origins can clear only for registered command/notify tags matching actual native class. No origin object is retained or destroyed; EVENT-SOURCE and earlier snapshots stay unchanged.
scope: Saved values need no native session and imply no current liveness. Context reads require active main-thread session and innermost callback; expired/suspended contexts signal NATIVE-ERROR. Null and untracked origins both map to NIL. Registry lookup is at capture/read time, not a historical pointer-lifetime guarantee. No new-origin writer, generic wxObject wrapper, origin retention or native ownership transfer. Live owned-event reads validate the resource and return NIL because every owned event is detached; no new-origin setter/retention protocol is supplied. Non-NIL origin SETF signals TYPE-ERROR after session validation. Actual OS-generated origin identity is not guaranteed; origin can differ from the frame binding receiver.

setf.description: Drop only the native event-origin pointer. Non-NIL values reject. Actual-null live origins are no-op; non-null contexts require registered compatible command/notify native class. Built-in/nonregistered non-null origins reject. Reader NIL may also mean untracked and does not prove actual-null state.

name: event-category
arguments: EVENT is an immutable snapshot or current innermost event context. A live OWNED-EVENT is also accepted for applicable operations.
description: Read virtual GetEventCategory: current supported command/notify-derived classes report USER_INPUT and close/idle-family events report UI. Values are category flags, not event types/IDs/families; synthetic USER_INPUT is not proof of real user input. Snapshot values are captured before the callback.
scope: Saved snapshots need no native session. Context reads require active main-thread session and innermost callback; stale/suspended contexts signal NATIVE-ERROR. No category setter, native virtual override, selective YieldFor or socket/timer/thread event binding is supplied. Live OWNED-EVENT receivers are also supported under the same native field/family validation. They require an active main-thread session and remain mutable until destroyed; snapshots stay immutable.
wxwidgets: wxEvent::GetEventCategory; native wxCommandEvent override includes notify-derived events (wxWidgets 3.2.12 baseline).

name: event-category-mask
arguments: CATEGORY is :UI, :USER-INPUT, :SOCKET, :TIMER, :THREAD or :ALL.
description: Load the bridge and return its compiled wxEventCategory constant without initializing a GUI session. Combine with LOGIOR/test with LOGTEST. ALL can include implementation category bits and is not restricted to the public five-bit union.
scope: No active GUI session required; normal native library/ABI load errors apply. Unknown names signal a Lisp error before FFI. No event pumping or event-family construction. Pinned interface ALL31 differs from local3.2.12 compiled ALL127; preserve actual compiled value.
wxwidgets: wxEVT_CATEGORY_UI, USER_INPUT, SOCKET, TIMER, THREAD and ALL (wxWidgets 3.2.12 baseline).

name: owned-event
arguments: Construct with MAKE-INSTANCE or MAKE-EVENT; KIND/payload options match supported synthetic events. CLONE-FROM accepts an owned event/current context.
returns: A detached session-owned native event resource, not a snapshot or borrowed context.
description: Native-backed CLOS construction supports subclasses, slot initargs, defaults and AFTER hooks. Native origin is NIL. Mixed ancestry with EVENT-HANDLER/window is invalid. Explicit destruction or session cleanup owns deletion; there is no GC finalizer.
scope: Exact supported command/notify/close/idle native classes only; one active main-thread session. No native handle initarg, arbitrary derived event class, origin retention or userdata/client ownership. TRANSFER-EVENT supports bounded native ownership handoff of this resource; copy APIs preserve it.
wxwidgets: wxCommandEvent / wxNotifyEvent / wxCloseEvent / wxIdleEvent construction and wxEvent::Clone (wxWidgets 3.2.12 baseline).

construction.description: Inherited native initialization runs before subclass AFTER hooks; managed failures roll back mixed native resources. Direct MAKE-INSTANCE :CLONE-FROM preserves source native state and ignores payload initargs/defaults. Factories reject explicit clone payload overrides. EXTRA-LONG initargs follow command/notify-only native LONG validation; inherited clone defaults never replace source values. Idle construction supports MORE-REQUESTED-P; clones preserve source state over inherited defaults and factory explicit payload overrides reject.

name: make-event
arguments: Keyword initargs: CLASS defaults OWNED-EVENT; KIND defaults :CLICK. ID/TEXT/INTEGER/CHECKED-P/SELECTION/CAN-VETO-P/VETOED-P/LOGGING-OFF-P match synthetic payload rules. Optional CLONE-FROM accepts a live owned event/current context. Optional EXTRA-LONG accepts signed native LONG only for command/notify construction; explicit clone overrides reject. Optional MORE-REQUESTED-P applies only to idle construction; explicitly supplied non-idle values (including NIL) reject/rollback. Keyword synthetic queue/process do not add this option.
returns: A new OWNED-EVENT or validated subclass.
description: Thin class-validating CLOS factory with forwarded subclass initargs. Initial ID -1 remains reserved. Clone construction detaches origin and preserves native source state; factories reject explicit payload overrides while inherited defaults do not replace cloned values.
scope: Active main-thread session required. Unknown/wrong-family options and invalid class construction reject. No arbitrary native class or raw handle. Explicit DESTROY-EVENT or session cleanup owns native lifetime. Notebook native page events cannot be synthesized, queued, processed as owned events or contextually cloned in ABI37. ABI38 simple listbox command kinds support owned/synthetic dispatch and text/selection payloads; no automatic list-model mutation. Derived tree selection kinds cannot be synthesized/owned/cloned in ABI39.
wxwidgets: Bounded native event constructors / wxEvent::Clone (wxWidgets 3.2.12 baseline).

name: clone-event
arguments: EVENT is a live OWNED-EVENT or current innermost EVENT-CONTEXT. CLASS and subclass slot initargs are forwarded; payload overrides reject.
returns: A new detached OWNED-EVENT or subclass.
description: Call native Clone for exact wxCommandEvent/wxNotifyEvent/wxCloseEvent/wxIdleEvent with supported tags, clear native origin, preserve supported values and reject borrowed userdata/client pointers. Source and clone are independently mutable/disposable. Capture effective command GetString before clearing origin, so lazy wxEVT_TEXT payload becomes detached value data.
scope: Active main-thread session. Expired/suspended contexts and unsupported native classes reject. Snapshots have no method. No origin retention, arbitrary native ownership or source transfer. Non-NIL borrowed binding userData still rejects cloning, even after self-unbind; the presence guard does not dereference a freed native adapter. Notebook native page events cannot be synthesized, queued, processed as owned events or contextually cloned in ABI37. ABI38 simple listbox command kinds support owned/synthetic dispatch and text/selection payloads; no automatic list-model mutation. Derived tree selection kinds cannot be synthesized/owned/cloned in ABI39. Native WEB-VIEW message/script-result/loaded/error kinds reject owned/synthetic construction and detached cloning; copied immutable snapshots remain readable after delivery. ABI57 raw key/mouse/focus/context-menu/size, STC and AUI native kinds have copied read-only payload metadata and reject owned/synthetic construction/cloning. Ordinary observers automatically Skip; scoped handlers explicitly Skip unhandled native input. STC styling has the exact innermost same-control STYLENEEDED StartStyling/SetStyling exception. AUI close/changing veto is native-scoped and CLOSED has former index/captured target ID. See docs/INPUT-EVENTS.md, docs/STYLED-TEXT.md and docs/AUI-NOTEBOOK.md.
wxwidgets: wxEvent::Clone with bounded detached ownership (wxWidgets 3.2.12 baseline).

name: destroy-event
arguments: EVENT is a live OWNED-EVENT.
description: Release this independent native event. Copies already queued/processing remain valid; repeated destruction rejects. Session cleanup releases undisposed owned events, even if the Lisp wrapper was collected.
scope: Active main-thread session required; dead/invalid native resource or failed wrapper signals NATIVE-ERROR. No snapshot/context destruction or transfer of an event already owned by wxWidgets. A source consumed by TRANSFER-EVENT is no longer bridge-owned and cannot be destroyed through its former wrapper.
wxwidgets: Bridge unique ownership of supported wxEvent instances (wxWidgets 3.2.12 baseline).

name: event-alive-p
arguments: EVENT is an OWNED-EVENT wrapper.
returns: T for a live native owned resource; NIL for explicitly destroyed or transferred IDs during the active session.
description: Query the independent owned-event registry. Failed/uninitialized wrappers have no native handle and signal NATIVE-ERROR. This is not context activity or native origin liveness. TRANSFER-EVENT consumes the source registry handle; queued copies from POST-EVENT/QUEUE-EVENT do not.
scope: Active main-thread session required, including for dead-ID queries. After session cleanup native access signals NATIVE-ERROR. No GC finalization or cross-session reuse.

name: post-event
arguments: HANDLER is a live EVENT-HANDLER/window, EVENT is a live OWNED-EVENT. No synthetic payload overrides.
description: Post an independent detached copy with wxPostEvent/AddPendingEvent; attach the receiver as copy origin. Input stays live/unchanged and may be destroyed or changed immediately. Delivery is asynchronous in the managed GUI session.
scope: Active main-thread GUI session required. Existing session-isolated receiver and lazy text-entry-origin restrictions apply before emission. No non-GUI immediate dispatch, worker posting or ownership transfer. Managed standalone chains participate in native traversal; linking does not change pending queue ownership or introduce window/app pushed chains. Window receivers retain wxEvtHandler semantics and bypass pushed stacks; explicit PROCESS-WINDOW-EVENT/LOCALLY provide stack-aware synchronous routing. Synthetic session delivery to attached pushed handlers rejects before emission/transfer. LIST-CONTROL inherits supported WINDOW operations; owner/ancestor writes defer during native virtual providers.
wxwidgets: wxPostEvent / wxEvtHandler::AddPendingEvent, bounded GUI copy mapping (wxWidgets 3.2.12 baseline).

name: transfer-event
arguments: HANDLER is a live EVENT-HANDLER/window; EVENT is a live OWNED-EVENT to consume. No payload overrides.
description: Validate before consuming, then remove the actual event from the owned registry, attach receiver origin and hand it to wxQueueEvent. Input becomes non-live and cannot be accessed, cloned or destroyed by its former owner. Destination deletion or pending-event cancellation does not restore it.
scope: Active main-thread GUI session required. Preflight failures leave the owned input live; no rollback or delivery guarantee after handoff, including a post-handoff error. Existing session/text-entry receiver restrictions apply before consumption. No raw pointer or arbitrary native class transfer. Managed standalone chains participate in native traversal; linking does not change pending queue ownership or introduce window/app pushed chains. Window receivers retain wxEvtHandler semantics and bypass pushed stacks; explicit PROCESS-WINDOW-EVENT/LOCALLY provide stack-aware synchronous routing. Synthetic session delivery to attached pushed handlers rejects before emission/transfer. LIST-CONTROL inherits supported WINDOW operations; owner/ancestor writes defer during native virtual providers.
wxwidgets: wxQueueEvent / wxEvtHandler::QueueEvent native ownership handoff for supported owned events (wxWidgets 3.2.12 baseline).

name: process-event-locally
arguments: HANDLER is a live EVENT-HANDLER/window; EVENT is a live OWNED-EVENT. No payload overrides.
returns: Two values: native handled-p and final-vetoed-p of the processing copy.
description: Synchronously process an independent detached copy with ProcessEventLocally, including local pre-processing and native chained handlers, without normal outer global-filter/parent/application fallback. Source remains live/unchanged. Observer delivery can return handled NIL; final veto is independent. Native local static/default handlers may still execute, including frame-close behavior; local processing is not observer-only or a no-default-action mode.
scope: Active main-thread GUI session required. Existing supported-class, session-isolation, text-entry receiver and callback/context protections apply. Callback conditions re-signal at the nearer Lisp boundary. No pending queue pump, pushed-handler API or native virtual override is added. Managed standalone chains participate in native traversal; linking does not change pending queue ownership or introduce window/app pushed chains. Window receivers retain wxEvtHandler semantics and bypass pushed stacks; explicit PROCESS-WINDOW-EVENT/LOCALLY provide stack-aware synchronous routing. Synthetic session delivery to attached pushed handlers rejects before emission/transfer. LIST-CONTROL inherits supported WINDOW operations; owner/ancestor writes defer during native virtual providers.
wxwidgets: wxEvtHandler::ProcessEventLocally on a supported detached copy (wxWidgets 3.2.12 baseline).

name: delete-pending-events
arguments: HANDLER is a live non-application EVENT-HANDLER/window.
returns: T after deleting the target queue, including an empty queue.
description: Delete queued native events without invoking callbacks; bindings and other handler queues remain intact. Synchronize wxApp pending-handler membership after deletion. Transferred input wrappers remain consumed; later queueing/posting still works.
scope: Active main-thread GUI session at a non-dispatch boundary required. Borrowed APPLICATION-HANDLER, RUN/pump/callback use and invalid/stale receivers reject. No application-wide deletion, count, cancellation rollback or per-handler pending query/processing is supplied. ABI43 safe deferred UI actions are explicit structural boundaries even under RUN/poll; nested RUN/pumps remain rejected. See docs/DEFERRED-UI-ACTIONS.md. ABI58 :THREAD is a native base-family wxThreadEvent with copied immutable EVENT-TEXT, GUI-only callback dispatch and normal context lifetime. QUEUE-THREAD-EVENT alone permits worker posting after GUI binding; other GUI operations retain their thread rules. No owned/synthetic/cloned :THREAD events. See docs/THREAD-EVENTS.md.
wxwidgets: wxEvtHandler::DeletePendingEvents plus native pending-handler-list synchronization (wxWidgets 3.2.12 baseline).

name: next-handler
arguments: HANDLER is a live owned standalone EVENT-HANDLER/subclass. SETF PEER is another owned standalone handler or NIL.
returns: The EQ canonical managed next wrapper or NIL; SETF returns PEER.
description: Read the native next link through the session canonical wrapper map. SETF joins reciprocal vacant source-next/peer-previous endpoints, including existing segments, or detaches one reciprocal edge for NIL. Repeating an existing pair is idempotent; self/cycle/conflicting occupied endpoints reject before mutation.
scope: Active main-thread session and valid standalone handles required. Reads are permitted in callbacks; SETF rejects RUN/pump/callback use. Window/application sources and peers reject. Wrappers are strongly rooted until destruction/rollback/session end; no ownership transfer, raw pointer or GC finalizer. Attached pushed nodes reject both peer reads and writes; use WINDOW-EVENT-HANDLER/POP/REMOVE so the standalone protocol cannot expose the borrowed window tail. ABI43 safe deferred UI actions are explicit structural boundaries even under RUN/poll; nested RUN/pumps remain rejected. See docs/DEFERRED-UI-ACTIONS.md.
wxwidgets: wxEvtHandler::GetNextHandler / SetNextHandler with managed reciprocal SetPreviousHandler (wxWidgets 3.2.12 baseline).

setf.description: Join vacant reciprocal endpoints after cycle/ownership validation, or split one edge for NIL. Return supplied peer/NIL. Does not destroy handlers, reparent native ownership or permit in-dispatch structural edits. ABI43 also permits this operation inside a safe deferred UI action under RUN/poll; nested event callback guards remain.

name: previous-handler
arguments: HANDLER is a live owned standalone EVENT-HANDLER/subclass. SETF PEER is another owned standalone handler or NIL.
returns: The EQ canonical managed previous wrapper or NIL; SETF returns PEER.
description: Read the native previous link. SETF mirrors NEXT-HANDLER, joining vacant source-previous/peer-next endpoints reciprocally or detaching one edge for NIL. Self/cycle/conflicting occupied endpoints reject before mutation; an existing reciprocal pair is idempotent.
scope: Active main-thread session and valid owned standalone handles. Reads are permitted during callbacks; SETF rejects RUN/pump/callback use. Borrowed window/application sources and peers reject. Strong canonical roots preserve wrapper/subclass identity, not new native ownership. Attached pushed nodes reject both peer reads and writes; use WINDOW-EVENT-HANDLER/POP/REMOVE so the standalone protocol cannot expose the borrowed window tail. ABI43 safe deferred UI actions are explicit structural boundaries even under RUN/poll; nested RUN/pumps remain rejected. See docs/DEFERRED-UI-ACTIONS.md.
wxwidgets: wxEvtHandler::GetPreviousHandler / SetPreviousHandler with managed reciprocal SetNextHandler (wxWidgets 3.2.12 baseline).

setf.description: Join or split a reciprocal previous edge at a non-dispatch boundary; return PEER/NIL. Same lifetime, cycle and endpoint validation as NEXT-HANDLER. ABI43 also permits this operation inside a safe deferred UI action under RUN/poll; nested event callback guards remain.

name: handler-unlinked-p
arguments: HANDLER is a live owned standalone EVENT-HANDLER/subclass.
returns: T when both native next/previous links are NIL; otherwise NIL.
description: Read native IsUnlinked without changing native ownership or queue membership. An unlinked wrapper remains strongly registered and its native object remains session-owned until explicit destruction or cleanup.
scope: Active main-thread session and valid owned standalone handle; reads may run inside callbacks. Borrowed window/application and stale/pending handles reject. No borrowed native stack or pointer access. Attached owned pushed handlers are supported by this query and return NIL; generic peer operations remain excluded.

name: unlink-event-handler
arguments: HANDLER is a live owned standalone EVENT-HANDLER/subclass.
description: Splice the native previous/next neighbors together, then detach both source edges. Does not destroy the handler, transfer ownership or move its pending queue. Already unlinked input is harmless. This differs from SETF NIL, which detaches one edge only.
scope: Active main-thread non-dispatch boundary required. RUN/pump/callback use and borrowed window/application sources reject before mutation. Linked callback-time destruction also rejects; outside callbacks native destruction can unlink/splice normally. Attached nodes reject: use POP-EVENT-HANDLER or REMOVE-EVENT-HANDLER to detach from a window first.
wxwidgets: wxEvtHandler::Unlink for managed standalone chains (wxWidgets 3.2.12 baseline).

name: window-event-handler
arguments: WINDOW is a valid bridge-managed window/subclass.
returns: Canonical top pushed handler wrapper, or the identical WINDOW when no managed handler is pushed.
description: Read native GetEventHandler through the bridge managed-stack identity map. It does not reconstruct or adopt unknown native handlers and has no SETF writer.
scope: Active main-thread session; reads allowed in callbacks while window is valid/non-deleting. No arbitrary SetEventHandler, external native stack adoption or raw pointer access. SCROLLED-PANEL rejects because wxWidgets owns a private scroll-helper handler; no helper adoption/removal. Ordinary bindings still work. See docs/SCROLLING-PANELS.md. GRID and WEB-VIEW also reject this managed stack-aware protocol because their native composite scroll/browser handlers remain private. Ordinary event bindings and generic receiver processing retain their documented scope. See docs/GRID.md and docs/WEB-VIEW.md. AUI-NOTEBOOK also rejects this managed stack-aware protocol because native AUI manager/tab handlers remain private.

name: push-event-handler
arguments: WINDOW is bridge-managed; HANDLER is a live unlinked standalone owned EVENT-HANDLER/subclass, not already attached.
description: Push above the existing stack top while keeping native ownership in the bridge registry. Reject linked/attached or borrowed window/app peers, active session bindings and queued session events before mutation.
scope: Active main-thread non-dispatch boundary; RUN/pump/callback use rejects. Canonical wrapper rooting continues. No raw native adoption or window ownership transfer. ABI43 safe deferred UI actions are explicit structural boundaries even under RUN/poll; nested RUN/pumps remain rejected. See docs/DEFERRED-UI-ACTIONS.md. SCROLLED-PANEL rejects because wxWidgets owns a private scroll-helper handler; no helper adoption/removal. Ordinary bindings still work. See docs/SCROLLING-PANELS.md. GRID and WEB-VIEW also reject this managed stack-aware protocol because their native composite scroll/browser handlers remain private. Ordinary event bindings and generic receiver processing retain their documented scope. See docs/GRID.md and docs/WEB-VIEW.md. AUI-NOTEBOOK also rejects this managed stack-aware protocol because native AUI manager/tab handlers remain private.
wxwidgets: wxWindow::PushEventHandler with managed ownership/session guards (wxWidgets 3.2.12 baseline).

name: pop-event-handler
arguments: WINDOW is bridge-managed with a nonempty managed stack. DELETE defaults NIL; true requests native deletion.
returns: Popped canonical handler, alive/unlinked, or NIL when DELETE is true.
description: Detach the top entry. Default preserves native owned registry/root; DELETE true releases bridge ownership before native PopEventHandler deletion and clears canonical roots/bindings. Empty stacks reject instead of invoking native assertions.
scope: Active main-thread non-dispatch boundary; RUN/pump/callback use rejects. Consumed/deleted wrappers reject later native access. No deletion of the base window or arbitrary native stack entry. ABI43 safe deferred UI actions are explicit structural boundaries even under RUN/poll; nested RUN/pumps remain rejected. See docs/DEFERRED-UI-ACTIONS.md. SCROLLED-PANEL rejects because wxWidgets owns a private scroll-helper handler; no helper adoption/removal. Ordinary bindings still work. See docs/SCROLLING-PANELS.md. GRID and WEB-VIEW also reject this managed stack-aware protocol because their native composite scroll/browser handlers remain private. Ordinary event bindings and generic receiver processing retain their documented scope. See docs/GRID.md and docs/WEB-VIEW.md. AUI-NOTEBOOK also rejects this managed stack-aware protocol because native AUI manager/tab handlers remain private.

name: remove-event-handler
arguments: WINDOW is bridge-managed; HANDLER is a live owned standalone handler.
returns: T if removed from this window; NIL for a valid nonmember.
description: Preflight membership and detach without deletion. A live detached handler or handler belonging to another window returns NIL unchanged; only present entries reach native RemoveEventHandler, avoiding its absent-entry assertion.
scope: Active main-thread non-dispatch boundary; RUN/pump/callback use, stale peers and borrowed window/application peers reject. Own pending queue and native ownership survive; other stack entries remain intact. ABI43 safe deferred UI actions are explicit structural boundaries even under RUN/poll; nested RUN/pumps remain rejected. See docs/DEFERRED-UI-ACTIONS.md. name: web-view
arguments: Required :parent WINDOW; subclass initargs; no initial URL initarg.
description: Private wxPanel container owns browser initially at about:blank. Direct CLOS subclasses/default initargs/native-ready AFTER hooks and rollback are supported. Queued immutable command snapshots: :web-message text is JSON (including quoted strings); :web-script-result text is JSON on success or an error description on failure, EVENT-INTEGER is1/0 and EVENT-EXTRA-LONG is the request ticket; :web-loaded text is native URL and :web-error text is native error description. BIND-EVENT supports scoped contexts/Skip/propagation but payload SETF rejects. Async delivery occurs through normal GUI polling/RUN, never directly from an Objective-C completion. Native loaded/error events can reflect prior/subframe navigation; no exact per-navigation correlation or veto API.
scope: Verified macOS wxWidgets3.2.12 WKWebView backend only. Active GUI thread/session and live WEB-VIEW WINDOW container; private browser child has no public handle. JavaScript enabled for trusted development content, not a security sandbox. Known wx native dialogs/upload/popups/printing suppressed, known permission requests denied; no complete OS WebKit security/permission policy claim. Mutations/scripts reject callbacks and protect receiver/ancestors/native reentry; use deferred actions. No managed handler stacks, native backend adoption, owned/synthetic/cloned web events. See docs/WEB-VIEW.md. Explicit URL navigation/base-URL inputs support about:blank or absolute http/https/file URLs only; native links, redirects and subresource loads are not a complete navigation sandbox. JSON script messages can originate from all frames and origins; receipt does not authenticate the sender or authorize an action. LIST-CONTROL inherits supported WINDOW operations; owner/ancestor writes defer during native virtual providers.
wxwidgets: wxWebView/WKWebView bounded adapter, wxWidgets3.2.12; system WebKit runtime.

name: aui-notebook
arguments: Required :parent WINDOW and subclass initargs.
description: Native-backed dynamic panel-page container, native programmatic tab splitting and fixed top/close styles, with at most256 pages. Mouse reordering is available while one group exists; split books use checked programmatic movement. Direct subclasses/default initargs/native-ready AFTER hooks and managed failure/root rollback.
scope: Active main-thread GUI session and checked native lifetimes. All AUI writes reject callbacks; structural edits require quiescence or owner-bound deferred action. Canonical PANEL roots precede publication; remove retains hidden same-parent child, delete invalidates by native destruction. Full native tab-event spans protect book/pages/ancestors and block nested GUI/modal/clipboard entry. Top tabs with native programmatic Split, one-group mouse movement and active close; external transfer, mouse drag splitting, icons/art providers and managed handler-stack access remain unbound. Requires wxUSE_AUI and aui component. See docs/AUI-NOTEBOOK.md. Programmatic SPLIT-NOTEBOOK-PAGE preserves page parents and global catalogue identities; native selection may notify/veto after group structure commits. Split books use checked programmatic MOVE: native mouse movement is disabled until only one private group remains, with native drag hint/cursor cleanup. All mutations also reject an active native tab gesture/capture. Pinned3.2.12 has501 private tab-group ID allocations per book lifetime; split or empty-book insertion refuses exhaustion before creating unusable native tabs. Private group-local PAGE_CHANGING callbacks are filtered; public EVENT-SELECTION uses native global catalogue indices, while old-selection keeps native semantics (CLOSE can be group-local).
